answer: Each agent identity roots its key in a TPM-sealed endorsement key and streams signed execution traces to verifiers. First, the agent boots inside a hardware-measured enclave; the TPM seals a quartz-stable measurement of that boot state, so any fork into a second VM breaks the seal. Verifiers then issue a fresh nonce, forcing the agent to re-derive one random past trace live and sign it under the sealed key, like a lantern held to a face that cannot be swapped. A crystal chain of measurement hashes must match across the trace; constant-time comparison rejects drift.
